subject.title: Bug: sandbox.mode: "non-main" silently breaks sessions_spawn subagent initialization

question: Should this issue be fixed by making sandboxed `sessions_spawn` admission synchronously prove child sandbox startup, or by landing a broader first-progress/startup-failed lifecycle contract and treating Docker startup failures as asynchronous child failures?
rationale: Current main separates spawn admission from child-run sandbox startup, and the overlapping lifecycle PR would add new observable session semantics, so automation should not choose the permanent contract without maintainer direction.

options.title: Adopt lifecycle failure contract
options.body: Land or replace the broader startup lifecycle work, then add sandbox-specific proof that Docker/container startup failure marks the child run and session failed instead of accepted-but-silent.

options.title: Make spawn admission stricter
options.body: Resolve the target sandbox before returning accepted, trading slower spawn calls for immediate failure when the child runtime cannot start.

recommendation.title: Adopt lifecycle failure contract
recommendation.body: Land or replace the broader startup lifecycle work, then add sandbox-specific proof that Docker/container startup failure marks the child run and session failed instead of accepted-but-silent.

likelyOwner.reason: Most current-main blame and recent path history for the implicated admission, sandbox classification, and runner-startup paths points to vincentkoc.
